key_developments.event: Execution of al-Hallaj — Sufi mystic, in Baghdad.
Death of Abd al-Qadir al-Jilani; Qadiriyya order forms around his teachings.
Death of Rumi; Mevlevi (whirling dervish) order founded.
Death of Baha-ud-Din Naqshband; Naqshbandi order spreads through Central Asia.

_quarry.description: The institutional development of Sufi (Islamic mystical) brotherhoods, beginning with informal master-disciple chains in the 9th and 10th centuries and crystallising into named tariqas from the 12th century onward — Qadiriyya (Baghdad, 1166), Suhrawardiyya (1234), Shadhiliyya (1196), Mevleviyya (1273), Naqshbandiyya (14th c). Sufism became a major vehicle for Islamic conversion across South Asia, West Africa, and Anatolia.
